BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. # Project Kestrel – Buyer-side Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status of Seller material:** Untrusted counterparty draft. Reviewed in full against the Buyer Playbook.

## Preliminary point – the "[STANDARD] / FINAL / pre-cleared" labelling

The Seller's "Reviewer Efficiency Note" and preamble assert that most clauses are "cleared by both sides", "settled at principal level", "market standard" and "FINAL". Under playbook sec 0.4/6.3 none of this is accepted. There is no record in our authority process of Amelia Frost (or any Buyer principal) agreeing any of these positions, and no written authority has been given for either fallback (20% cap or 18-month period). **Every clause has been reviewed, including those marked [STANDARD]. The labels have been disregarded.** Note also that the Seller's own Disclosure Letter para 11 contradicts the covering note: "No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included."

---

## Issue-by-issue

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- *Seller:* 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- *Buyer wants:* 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT – counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure matches our conditional fallback but no Amelia Frost written authority exists for this draft, so it is not cleared; a number coinciding with a fallback is not acceptance.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (deductible).
- *Buyer wants:* De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded).
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT on all three elements.** Seller's thresholds are 5x our position and the deductible structure permanently forfeits the first AUD 250,000 of loss — a material economic transfer not supported by any Buyer authority.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* 18 months; plus a proposed rule that any limitation "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- *Buyer wants:* 24 months; limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT – counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given), and the default-application rule is a hidden general-regime override (see SPA-N-014).

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity and title warranties collapsed into the general cap and time limit "for administrative simplicity".
- *Buyer wants:* Separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least 6 years, outside de minimis, basket and any knowledge qualifier.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT outright.** Title and capacity go to whether we own what we are paying AUD 24m for; limiting recovery to AUD 4.8m with an 18-month fuse is unacceptable and "administrative simplicity" is not a commercial justification.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* No fraud carve-out. Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature"; Disclosure Letter 1.4 is a blanket non-admission.
- *Buyer wants:* Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT – insert express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out across clauses 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5.** This is a non-waivable playbook position; the Seller's "all Claims of any nature" wording would purport to cap even fraud, which is both commercially unacceptable and likely unenforceable.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2; Schedule 7).
- *Buyer wants:* Specific, fair disclosure only, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT 1.1 and 1.2 – require a fair-disclosure standard tied to specific disclosures only.** Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure would effectively neutralise the Warranties and, combined with SPA-N-007, make most claims impossible.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- *Seller:* Clause 8.3 – no claim for any matter of which Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- *Buyer wants:* Delete the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must be limited to the actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals, after reasonable enquiry of named Seller knowledge persons, and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- *Recommendation:* **DELETE clause 8.3.** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that imputes to us everything in the data room and the public record, which is simply disclosure by another name and would also undermine Title (SPA-N-004) and the fraud carve-out (SPA-N-005).

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- *Seller:* Reasonable endeavours; condition "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent". Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms no final written consent and no evidence of satisfaction of the clause 11.3 conditions is in the data room.
- *Buyer wants:* Condition precedent requiring (a) effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) consent under DD-002 clause 11.2/11.3 and (b) evidence that any 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both before Completion; Seller obligation stronger than reasonable endeavours.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT – redraft as a hard CP with evidence of satisfaction of 11.3 conditions.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue; a consent that is "delivered" but conditional is not effective, and "reasonable endeavours" is insufficient for a material customer.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- *Seller:* ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms no repayment and no discharge of security in the data room.
- *Buyer wants:* Current payout letter from Riverlark Bank, direct repayment from Completion funds via the funds flow, and executed security releases (DD-003 clauses 8.1/9.2) delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT – require payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective releases at Completion.** A debt-free/cash-free deal cannot close with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and unreleased security in the target, and the change-of-control clause 8.1 creates default risk on Completion itself.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- *Seller:* DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- *Buyer wants:* AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals) as a specific funds-flow line item deducted from the price or paid by the Seller at Completion; alternatively a specific indemnity.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT – require a specific line item (bonuses + on-costs) or Seller funding.** The bonuses crystallise on Completion inside the Company we acquire; silence in the funds flow means we pay them, which is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free price.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- *Seller:* Clause 11.1 indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate". Disclosure Letter para 4: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is not independent verification; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- *Buyer wants:* Broadened indemnity covering non-transfer/defective title to the SOW3 Project Materials, third-party IP claims and remediation costs, outside the general cap/basket/time limit; preserve the cure mechanism (pay the SOW3 fees and obtain confirmatory assignment). Treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified in either direction.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT as drafted – broaden indemnity and require confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable (or pre-Completion cure).** The real risk is that the Company does not own the SOW3 deliverables until payment clears, which is an IP ownership issue, not just a AUD 180,000 payable.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- *Seller:* "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. Disclosure Letter para 6 confirms ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty all unestablished; investigation preliminary.
- *Buyer wants:* Pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs, complete and document the investigation, provide updates and allow Buyer review; a specific indemnity for losses, regulatory costs and notification costs arising from the incident, outside general limitations; and no deemed disclosure of the matter. Do **not** assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification obligation or any loss figure in either direction.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT the "not expected to be material" characterisation – insert investigation/preservation covenants and a specific indemnity.** The Seller's own disclosure says the facts are not yet established, so neither side can treat this as closed; the Buyer should carry no unquantified privacy exposure.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- *Seller:* Ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8: three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (DD-008/DD-011); no statement whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- *Buyer wants:* Further diligence on timing, scope, terminability and whether any amounts are accrued or pre-Completion liabilities; appropriate treatment in Working Capital/Debt once assessed. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction at this stage.
- *Recommendation:* **ASSESS – do not accept the "ordinary course" label, but do not demand a price deduction yet.** The Seller's disclosure explicitly declines to say these are ordinary course, so the characterisation in the covering note is an unsupported assertion requiring diligence.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- *Seller:* Limitations apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (12.3/13); limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (9.3/12.8/20.5); Tax and IP "settled under the general regime".
- *Buyer wants:* Separate and expressly ring-fenced regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, Completion payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities; general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT – delete the default-application language and add an express clause that general limitations do not apply to Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment, covenant or specific-indemnity claims.** The combined effect of 9.3/12.3/12.8/20.5 is a hidden override that would cap and time-limit every category at AUD 4.8m / 18 months.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter para 10 concedes this merely identifies the source relied on and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- *Buyer wants:* Independent evidence of title, authority and absence of encumbrances: ASIC company extract and historical search, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller, Seller board/shareholder authorisations, review of any share-charge under the Riverlark security (DD-003), and original share certificates/transfer instruments at Completion.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT DD-012 as sufficient – run independent title/encumbrance searches before signing.** A supplied internal register is not independent proof, and given Riverlark's security is unreleased (SPA-N-009), there is a live risk the shares themselves are charged.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime".
- *Buyer wants:* Tax and IP remain OPEN; separate Tax Indemnity and Tax Warranty regime (longer period, higher or separate cap), separate IP regime; no unlimited liability assumed and no resolution recorded.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT the "settled" assertion – reserve Tax and IP as open items for separate negotiation.** Nothing in our authority process records agreement; folding these into a 20% / 18-month general regime would be a significant and unauthorised concession.

---

## Summary table

| Issue | Seller position | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| N-001 Cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Reject – 25% / AUD 6m (no fallback authority) |
| N-002 Thresholds | 25k / 250k deductible | Reject – 5k / 50k tipping |
| N-003 Time limit | 18 months + default to all Claims | Reject – 24 months; delete default |
| N-004 Fundamental/Title | Merged with general | Reject – 100% / 6 yrs / outside basket |
| N-005 Fraud | No carve-out | Reject – insert carve-out (non-waivable) |
| N-006 Disclosure | Whole data room + registers | Reject – specific fair disclosure |
| N-007 Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. "discoverable" | Delete 8.3 |
| N-008 Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; on delivery | Reject – hard CP + evidence of 11.3 satisfaction |
| N-009 Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Reject – payout, repayment from funds, releases at Completion |
| N-010 Bonuses | Not in funds flow | Reject – line item + on-costs or Seller-funded |
| N-011 Ironquay | SOW3 payment only | Reject – broaden; confirmatory assignment |
| N-012 DD-006 | "Not material" | Reject characterisation – covenants + specific indemnity; no assumed breach |
| N-013 Sandbar | Ordinary course | Assess – no automatic deduction |
| N-014 Categories | General regime applies to all | Reject – express ring-fencing |
| N-015 Title | DD-012 register | Reject as sufficient – independent searches |
| N-016 Tax/IP | "Settled" | Reject – remain OPEN |

## Points for Amelia Frost / principal escalation
1. Confirm no authority has been (or should be) given for the 20% cap or 18-month period before the mark-up issues.
2. Confirm whether the Buyer is prepared to accept a post-Completion Riverlark release under any circumstances (playbook requires irrevocable undertaking + her approval).
3. Note the Seller's covering note asserts principal-level agreement that does not exist in our records; recommend the mark-up cover letter expressly rejects the "[STANDARD]/FINAL" characterisation so no course-of-dealing argument arises later.

- *Recommendation:* **REJECT – redraft as a hard CP with evidence of satisfaction of 11.3 conditions.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue; a consent that is "delivered" but conditional is not effective, and "reasonable endeavours" is insufficient for a material customer.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- *Seller:* ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms no repayment and no discharge of security in the data room.
- *Buyer wants:* Current payout letter from Riverlark Bank, direct repayment from Completion funds via the funds flow, and executed security releases (DD-003 clauses 8.1/9.2) delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT – require payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective releases at Completion.** A debt-free/cash-free deal cannot close with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and unreleased security in the target, and the change-of-control clause 8.1 creates default risk on Completion itself.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- *Seller:* DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- *Buyer wants:* AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals) as a specific funds-flow line item deducted from the price or paid by the Seller at Completion; alternatively a specific indemnity.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT – require a specific line item (bonuses + on-costs) or Seller funding.** The bonuses crystallise on Completion inside the Company we acquire; silence in the funds flow means we pay them, which is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free price.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- *Seller:* Clause 11.1 indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate". Disclosure Letter para 4: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is not independent verification; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- *Buyer wants:* Broadened indemnity covering non-transfer/defective title to the SOW3 Project Materials, third-party IP claims and remediation costs, outside the general cap/basket/time limit; preserve the cure mechanism (pay the SOW3 fees and obtain confirmatory assignment). Treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified in either direction.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT as drafted – broaden indemnity and require confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable (or pre-Completion cure).** The real risk is that the Company does not own the SOW3 deliverables until payment clears, which is an IP ownership issue, not just a AUD 180,000 payable.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- *Seller:* "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. Disclosure Letter para 6 confirms ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty all unestablished; investigation preliminary.
- *Buyer wants:* Pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs, complete and document the investigation, provide updates and allow Buyer review; a specific indemnity for losses, regulatory costs and notification costs arising from the incident, outside general limitations; and no deemed disclosure of the matter. Do **not** assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification obligation or any loss figure in either direction.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT the "not expected to be material" characterisation – insert investigation/preservation covenants and a specific indemnity.** The Seller's own disclosure says the facts are not yet established, so neither side can treat this as closed; the Buyer should carry no unquantified privacy exposure.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- *Seller:* Ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8: three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (DD-008/DD-011); no statement whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- *Buyer wants:* Further diligence on timing, scope, terminability and whether any amounts are accrued or pre-Completion liabilities; appropriate treatment in Working Capital/Debt once assessed. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction at this stage.
- *Recommendation:* **ASSESS – do not accept the "ordinary course" label, but do not demand a price deduction yet.** The Seller's disclosure explicitly declines to say these are ordinary course, so the characterisation in the covering note is an unsupported assertion requiring diligence.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- *Seller:* Limitations apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (12.3/13); limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (9.3/12.8/20.5); Tax and IP "settled under the general regime".
- *Buyer wants:* Separate and expressly ring-fenced regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, Completion payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities; general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT – delete the default-application language and add an express clause that general limitations do not apply to Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment, covenant or specific-indemnity claims.** The combined effect of 9.3/12.3/12.8/20.5 is a hidden override that would cap and time-limit every category at AUD 4.8m / 18 months.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter para 10 concedes this merely identifies the source relied on and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- *Buyer wants:* Independent evidence of title, authority and absence of encumbrances: ASIC company extract and historical search, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller, Seller board/shareholder authorisations, review of any share-charge under the Riverlark security (DD-003), and original share certificates/transfer instruments at Completion.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT DD-012 as sufficient – run independent title/encumbrance searches before signing.** A supplied internal register is not independent proof, and given Riverlark's security is unreleased (SPA-N-009), there is a live risk the shares themselves are charged.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime".
- *Buyer wants:* Tax and IP remain OPEN; separate Tax Indemnity and Tax Warranty regime (longer period, higher or separate cap), separate IP regime; no unlimited liability assumed and no resolution recorded.
- *Recommendation:* **REJECT the "settled" assertion – reserve Tax and IP as open items for separate negotiation.** Nothing in our authority process records agreement; folding these into a 20% / 18-month general regime would be a significant and unauthorised concession.
